headline: Aspinall’s 170 checkout seals 10-7 win over Clemens
standfirst: Nathan Aspinall hit the biggest finish in darts to break for a 9-6 lead and beat Gabriel Clemens, matching his run to the Grand Slam quarter-finals in 2020.
body: Nathan Aspinall is into the Grand Slam of Darts quarter-finals, matching his run in 2020, after beating Gabriel Clemens 10-7, and the moment that settled it was a 170 checkout.

At 6-5 down, Aspinall won four legs in a row. The fourth was the big one: a 170 finish in 12 darts to break Clemens’ throw and lead 9-6, leaving the German needing to win four straight. Clemens took one back before Aspinall broke again to finish it.

His finishing was the story of the match. Aspinall converted 52.6 per cent of his attempts at a double, against 31.8 for Clemens, and broke throw five times. His 100.72 average was more than four points above his 12-month figure of 96.5.

Clemens outscored him on maximums, hitting ten 180s to Aspinall’s seven, the most by anyone on Thursday night, and averaged 96.55. It was his best Grand Slam run on the PDC’s records, having previously gone out in the group stage.
Aspinall plays Gian van Veen on Saturday at 8:45pm, a meeting of two players who have both spoken about coming through dartitis.
